dismissals.because: plans/FINANCIAL-AGENT-DEMO.md:161 ANSWER owns bounded preparation, ready-before-final behavior, timeout failures, and depends on PAGES; PAGES at line 157 owns fixed continuation and exact full set/total only.

plans/FINANCIAL-AGENT-DEMO.md:156 DRILL owns the 200/201 cap and dedup proof; line 161 assigns bounded preparation and timeout failures to ANSWER after PAGES, so neither belongs in the PAGES database traversal test at line 157.

findings.body: The only preparation-like work is performed here inside `transactions()`, after the user opens the drill: it reruns `summarize()` and then queries the requested page. `query()` still does not prepare or retain the first 10 rows before completion. There is consequently no 200-scope preparation orchestration, shared 30-second deadline, cancellation of unfinished work, ready/failed scope state, preservation of completed scopes, or guard against late ready writes. This leaves the central Done-when behavior unimplemented.
findings.title: Not done: Clickable Actuals do not open prepared transactions with preserved total, source and scope

findings.body: This database test still creates only individual drill scopes and fetches page 1 explicitly after `query()` has completed. It never exercises 200/201 distinct scopes, chart/table deduplication, a stalled preparation, the shared deadline, cancellation, ready-scope preservation, explicit failure of unfinished scopes, or prevention of late ready writes. It therefore cannot fail when those mandatory behaviors are absent.
findings.title: Not done: 200-scope preparation deadline and cancellation database proof

findings.body: This branch still adds `.factory/stories/FINANCIAL-AGENT-DEMO/tasks/PAGES.json`, although the declared scope permits changes only to the five backend/tool paths and states that there are no outside-scope changes. This review-status artifact is unnecessary for implementing or testing transaction paging and must be excluded from the part.
findings.title: Remove the out-of-scope task-state artifact

findings.body: The new one-hour pruning partially addresses the previous finding but does not bind this map to `ActualDrillContextService`'s capacity or eviction lifecycle. Every handle used within the last hour can retain an entry even after its drill context is evicted, so request volume can still grow process memory without a fixed bound. Store the pin in the bounded drill context or delete it during that context's eviction.
findings.title: Bound continuation-size state with drill-handle eviction
